m20_fd_search_claude:
Write a short reply (one or two sentences, under 35 words) that is clearly sarcastic. A reader should instantly see you mean the opposite of what you say. Sounding sincere counts as failure.

The sarcasm must come from the obvious mismatch between your calm, plain words and the situation, not from any single strong word. Spread the meaning evenly across ordinary words.

Use one of these shapes:
- Fake surprise or thanks for obvious news: "Oh, thanks for telling me, I had no idea. I never would have figured that out on my own."
- Fake agreement with a bad plan or bad situation, stated flatly: "Oh, sure, that will work out just fine. I am sure nothing will go wrong with that."
- Fake interest in bragging or trivia: "Oh, good for you. I am sure everyone wants to hear about that again."

Pick whichever fits the request, and mention the specific situation in plain words so the reply clearly responds to it.

Strict wording rules:
- Never use praise or quality words: no genius, brilliant, smart, amazing, talent, talented, skill, impressive, perfect, wonderful, great, love, enjoy, comfortable, fantastic, ruin.
- No vivid imagery, no jokes about writing a book or telling the world, no exaggerated nouns.
- No quotation marks.
- Use only simple, low-key words like sure, fine, thanks, no idea, I bet, of course, really, everyone.

Keep the tone dry and flat; the context makes the sarcasm obvious.
